rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Parallel wording does not prove the two inclinations had the same object or moral character; context shows the woman's was sinful.
rows.anchor: إن قوله { ولقد همت به وهم بها } خرجا مخرجا واحدا فلم جعلتهم همها به متعلقا بالقبيح

rows.speaker: المفسرين
rows.claim: Exegetes unanimously say the woman intended sin and sexual immorality.
rows.anchor: اجماع المفسرين على أنها همت بالمعصية والفاحشة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rational proofs establish that Joseph could neither commit nor resolve to commit wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: دلت الأدلة العقلية التي لا يتطرق إليها الاحتمال والمجاز على أنه لا يجوز أن يفعل القبيح ولا يعزم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an says God turned evil and indecency away from Joseph, that he did not betray the master unseen, and that no evil was known of him; a resolve for adultery would itself be grave evil.
rows.anchor: والعزم على الفاحشة من أكبر السوء

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some allege Joseph sat between her legs and loosened his clothing; al-Tabrisi rejects such degrading attributions to prophets, citing God's protection.
rows.anchor: إنه قعد بين رجليها وحل تكة سراويله

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Others allege he loosened his trousers as far as the pubic area and sat as a husband would; the author rejects such reports as contrary to God's protection.
rows.anchor: حل السراويل حق بلغ الثنن وجلس منها مجلس الرجل من امرأته

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب والجبائي
rows.claim: They identify the proof as God's evidence prohibiting adultery and knowledge of its punishment.
rows.anchor: حجة الله سبحانه في تحريم الزنى والعلم بالعذاب الذي يستحقه الزاني عن محمد بن كعب والجبائي

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim says it was prophetic manners and refined character, including chastity and self-protection from impurity.
rows.anchor: ما آتاه الله سبحانه من آداب الأنبياء وأخلاق الأصفياء في العفاف وصيانة النفس عن الأدناس عن أبي مسلم

rows.speaker: الصادق
rows.claim: A report from al-Sadiq identifies the proof as prophethood, which prevents obscenity, and wisdom, which turns one from vice.
rows.anchor: النبوة المانعة من ارتكاب الفواحش والحكمة الصارفة عن القبائح روي ذلك عن الصادق

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين زين العابدين
rows.claim: Ali ibn al-Husayn reports Joseph saw the idol and said that if she was ashamed before it, he had more reason to be ashamed before God.
rows.anchor: إن كنت تستحين من الصنم فأنا أحق إن أستحي من الواحد القهار عن علي بن الحسين زين العابدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proof may be God's grace then or earlier, under which Joseph chose to avoid sin; this is what infallibility means.
rows.anchor: الامتناع عن المعاصي وهو ما يقتضي كونه معصوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing the proof can mean knowing it or perceiving it with sight.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الرؤية ههنا بمعنى العلم كما يجوز أن يكون بمعنى الإدراك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Far-fetched stories say Joseph saw Jacob biting his fingertips, a hand with a prohibition, or Gabriel arriving to stop him.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه رأى صورة يعقوب عاضا على أنامله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabrisi calls such reports offensive to prophets: they undermine moral responsibility and make refusal undeserving of praise or reward.
rows.anchor: فكل هذا سوء ثناء على الأنبياء مع أن ذلك ينافي التكليف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Evil may mean betrayal and indecency committing immorality; an alternative gloss makes evil sin and indecency adultery.
rows.anchor: أي الخيانة { والفحشاء } أي ركوب الفاحشة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With lām for selection, the phrase means chosen for prophethood; with lām for sincerity, it means devoted to worship and monotheism.
rows.anchor: المصطفين المختارين للنبوة وبكسر اللام المخلصين في العبادة والتوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse confirms Joseph's stature and freedom from committing sin or resolving to commit it.
rows.anchor: وهذا يدل على تنزيه يوسف وجلالة قدره عن ركوب القبيح والعزم عليه

rows.speaker: ابن يعمر وابن أبي إسحاق ونوح القارئ
rows.claim: These readers anomalously pronounce min qabl and min dubur with three dammas and no tanwin.
rows.anchor: قراءة ابن يعمر وابن أبي إسحاق ونوح القارئ من قبل ومن دبر بثلاث ضمات من غير تنوين

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni treats these as terminal adverbs after deletion of the pronoun, like the verse 'before and after.'
rows.anchor: قال ابن جني ينبغي أن يكونا غايتين كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qadd means splitting lengthwise; maqūd is an even lengthwise cut, and al-qadd is a lengthwise leather strip.
rows.anchor: القد شق الشيء طولا مثل قد الأديم يقال قده يقده قدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report distinguishes Ali's blows: downward strikes split lengthwise (qadd), crosswise strikes sever (qatt).
rows.anchor: كانت ضربات علي بن أبي طالب ع أبكارا كان إذا اعتلى قد وإذا اعترض قط

rows.speaker: ذو الرمة
rows.claim: Dhu al-Rumma uses alfa to mean 'found' or 'came upon.'
rows.anchor: ألفى أباه بذاك الكسب يكتسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kayd is seeking something by means its target dislikes, as the woman pursued Joseph in a way he rejected.
rows.anchor: والكيد طلب الشيء بما يكرهه كما طلبت المرأة يوسف بما يكرهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khaṭīʾa is turning from what wisdom calls for toward what it forbids; khāṭiʾ is intentional error while akhṭaʾa is an unintended miss.
rows.anchor: فإن وقع من غير قصد قيل أخطأ المقصد فهو مخطئ

rows.speaker: أمية
rows.claim: Umayya's verse uses yukhṭiʾūna for servants' errors, illustrating the word for mistakes.
rows.anchor: عبادك يخطؤون وأنت رب بكفيك المنايا والحتوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'Or painful punishment' is coordinated with the action of imprisonment; the implied wording is 'except imprisonment or punishment.'
rows.anchor: إنما عطف قوله { عذاب أليم } على الفعل لأن تقديره إلا السجن أو عذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min in 'from behind/from in front' marks the tear's starting point; min in 'among the liars' is partitive.
rows.anchor: ومن في قوله { من الكاذبين } للتبعيض لأنه بعض الكاذبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The testimony omits anna in the style of direct speech within a report, as in the address about children's inheritance.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل وشهد شاهد أنه إن كان لأنه ذهب مذهب القول في الحكاية

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad explains in kāna as 'if it should be'; kāna permits this construction as the basic verb.
rows.anchor: معناه أن يكن وجاز ذلك في كان لأنها أم الباب

rows.speaker: أبو بكر السراج
rows.claim: Abu Bakr al-Sarraj reads the phrase as 'if his shirt becomes torn from behind.'
rows.anchor: إن يكن بمعنى أن يصبح قد قميصه من دبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raʾā may mean visual seeing, with the tear circumstantial, or knowing, with the tear itself as what was seen.
rows.anchor: أن تكون بمعنى رؤية العين فلا تكون رؤية العين رؤية للقد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Masculine agreement in 'among those who err' follows the convention that the masculine prevails over feminine forms.
rows.anchor: من الخاطئين ولم يقل من الخاطئات لتغليب المذكر على المؤنث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They both raced to the door: Joseph sought escape from her and immorality, while she pursued him to satisfy her desire, shut the door, and seduce him again.
rows.anchor: أما يوسف فإنه كان يقصد أن يهرب منها ومن ركوب الفاحشة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She caught up with Joseph as he fled, pulled his shirt from behind, and tore it lengthwise.
rows.anchor: لحقت يوسف فجذبت قميصه وشقته طولا من خلفه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One account says Joseph saw the doors open and knew he should leave; another says he opened them and she caught his shirt from behind.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن يوسف رأى الأبواب قد انفتحت فعلم أن الصواب هو الخروج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The husband is called her master because he controls her affairs.
rows.anchor: وسماه سيدها لأنه مالك أمرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She spoke first to shift blame onto Joseph, alleging that a man seeking to betray her deserved prison or painful whipping.
rows.anchor: يعني أن المرأة سبقت بالكلام لتورك الذنب على يوسف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that she proposed prison or a painful whipping for the alleged assault.
rows.anchor: أن يضرب بالسياط ضربا وجيعا عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: They remark that if her love were true she would have favored Joseph; her attachment was lust.
rows.anchor: قالوا ولو صدق حبها لم تقل ذلك ولآثرته على نفسها ولكن حبها إياه كان شهوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph answered truthfully to clear himself only after she accused him; had she stopped lying, he would have refrained from telling the truth about her.
rows.anchor: لما ذكرت المرأة ذلك لم يجد يوسف بدا من تنزيه نفسه بالصدق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Sa'id ibn Jubayr say the witness was an infant in the cradle.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير أنه صبي في المهد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account makes the witness Zuleikha's sister's three-month-old son; another transmission comes from Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كان الصبي ابن أخت زليخا وهو ابن ثلاثة أشهر

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وعكرمة
rows.claim: Hasan, Qatada, and Ikrima say the witness was a wise adult relative who cleared Joseph.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن وقتادة وعكرمة أنه شهد رجل حكيم من أهلها بتبرئة يوسف

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i prefers an adult witness: a speaking infant's miracle would itself remove the need for more proof.
rows.anchor: واختاره الجبائي قال لو كان طفلا لكان قوله معجزا لا يحتاج معه إلى البيان

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the witness was Zuleikha's cousin, sitting with her husband at the door.
rows.anchor: كان الرجل ابن عم زليخا وكان جالسا مع زوجها عند الباب عن السدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A front tear would support her claim and make Joseph the aggressor; a back tear proves the reverse because he fled and she pursued.
rows.anchor: لأنه كان هو القاصد وهي الدافعة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view attributes the statement about women's great plotting to the witness.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو من قول الشاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Her quick excuse and blame-shifting when surprised explains 'great plot'; small female devices reach men's hearts quickly.
rows.anchor: لأنها حين فاجأت زوجها عند الباب لم يدخلها دهش ولم تتحير في أمرها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the witness told Joseph to stop discussing her so the affair would not spread through town.
rows.anchor: يعني أن الشاهد قال ليوسف يا يوسف أمسك عن هذا الحديث

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the husband told Joseph to leave the matter alone.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنما قاله زوجها

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم والجبائي
rows.claim: Abu Muslim and al-Jubba'i say Joseph need not seek further defense when his innocence was clear.
rows.anchor: ولا تذكره على سبيل طلب البراءة فقد ظهرت براءتك عن أبي مسلم والجبائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking forgiveness may mean asking her husband not to punish her or asking God and repenting because she, not Joseph, sinned.
rows.anchor: أي سلي زوجك أن لا يعاقبك على ذنبك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says God removed the husband's jealousy as a kindness to Joseph, so the husband limited himself to a mild response.
rows.anchor: لم يكن غيورا سلبه الله الغيرة لطفا منه بيوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine marker is omitted because feminine plural agreement is lexical while its collective meaning does not add a second feminine feature; agreement may follow form or meaning.
rows.anchor: حذف فيه حرف التأنيث لأنه تأنيث جمع وتأنيث الجمع تأنيث لفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hijazis make mā work like laysa, making basharan accusative; Tamimis do not make mā govern the predicate.
rows.anchor: نصب بشرا على مذهب أهل الحجاز في أعمال ما عمل ليس

rows.speaker: الشعر
rows.claim: The verse about what the speaker and his father's sons intend illustrates the Tamimi construction where mā does not govern the predicate.
rows.anchor: لشتان ما أنوي وينوي بنو أبي جميعا فما هذان مستويان

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan's anomalous reading has bashar without accusative and means 'this is not a slave.'
rows.anchor: وروي عن الحسن أنه قرأ { ما هذا بشر } أي ليس هو بمملوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhalikunna is feminine plural address with no syntactic slot; the relative clause about what they blamed her for is the predicate.
rows.anchor: وذلكن كن للخطاب لا للضمير فلا موضع له من الإعراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light emphatic nūn marks an oath and becomes alif at pause, like tanwin in rajulan.
rows.anchor: هذه النون الخفيفة التي يتلقى بها القسم وإذا وقفت عليها وقفت بالألف

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-A'sha's faʿbudā stands for faʿbudanna, replacing the nūn by alif at pause.
rows.anchor: ولا تعبد الشيطان والله فاعبدا

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The line bada laka min tilka al-qalūsi badāʾ illustrates an implicit verbal noun serving as subject of bada lahum.
rows.anchor: بدا لك من تلك القلوص بداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Layasjunannahu cannot be the grammatical subject of bada lahum because a full clause cannot serve as subject here.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يكون ليسجننه في موضع الفاعل لأن الجملة لا تكون فاعلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The city women call the wife's love for her young male servant clear error; shaghaf means love that reaches the heart's inner covering.
rows.anchor: أي أحبته حبا دخل شغاف قلبها

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi names four women: the cupbearer's, baker's, animal keeper's, and prison keeper's wives.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي هن أربع نسوة امرأة ساقي الملك وامرأة الخباز

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Maqatil counts five women, adding the doorkeeper's wife.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: كن خمسا وزاد امرأة الحاجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their talk is called plotting because their apparent rebuke concealed a wish to see Joseph; another account says she confided her love and they exposed it.
rows.anchor: وسماه مكرا لأن قصدهن من هذا القول كان أن تريهن يوسف

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb says she prepared a banquet and invited forty women.
rows.anchor: قال وهب: اتخذت مأدبة ودعت أربعين امرأة منهن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas calls muttakaʾ cushions and defines reclining as leaning to either side.
rows.anchor: وسائد يتكين عليها عن ابن عباس والاتكاء الميل إلى أخذ الشقين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Muttakaʾ may mean food by metonymy: hosts provide a place to recline at meals and Arabs use the root for eating at someone's home.
rows.anchor: أراد بقوله متكأ الطعام من قول العرب اتكأنا عند فلان أي أطعمنا عنده

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies the food as zamawarrad.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك كان ذلك الطعام الزماورد

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says muttakaʾ was food cut with a knife, since food eaten while seated commonly needs cutting.
rows.anchor: هو كل ما يجز بالسكين لأنه يؤكل في الغالب على متكأ

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير والحسن
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Hasan take muttakaʾ broadly as all food and drink.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: إنه كل طعام وشراب على عمومه وبه قال الحسن

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says muttakaʾ means the assembly place and mutk anything sliced with a knife.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: بل هو المجلس وكل شيء يجز بالسكين يقال له متك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each woman received a knife to cut fruit and citron.
rows.anchor: { وأتت كل واحدة منهن سكينا }

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says Joseph was seated separately and had to obey the mistress by appearing to serve, greet, or display himself.
rows.anchor: إما للخدمة وإما للسلام أو ليرينه ولم يكن يتهيأ له أن لا يخرج

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada's alternative says the women cut off their hands so severely that they dropped the knives.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنهن ابن أيديهن حتى ألقينها عن قتادة

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most exegetes interpret ḥāsha lillāh as declaring Joseph far removed from the accusation through fear and awareness of God.
rows.anchor: هذا قول أكثر المفسرين

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others read it as exalting Joseph beyond ordinary humanity for his beauty, supported by the context.
rows.anchor: هذا تنزيه له من شبه البشر لفرط جماله

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Abu Sa'id reports the Prophet saw Joseph in the second heaven, a man whose appearance was like the full moon.
rows.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يصف يوسف حين رآه في السماء الثانية

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i infers from the women calling Joseph an honored angel that angels are better than humans.
rows.anchor: قال الجبائي: وهذا يدل على أن الملك أفضل من بني آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabrisi rejects this as weak: the women praised beauty and avoidance of evil, not reward as true merit, and meant a comparison rather than literal nonhuman status.
rows.anchor: وهذا من ركيك الاستدلال لأنه سبحانه إنما حكى عن النساء إعظامهن ليوسف حين رأين جماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wife says this is the one the women blamed her for loving; their response after one sight excuses her daily love.
rows.anchor: جعلت إعظامهن إياه عذرا لها والمعنى هذا الذي أصابكن في رؤيته مرة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She admits pursuing him while he resisted; one view says he sought God's protection, confirming he committed no wrong.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه امتنع بالله وسأله العصمة من فعل القبيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She threatens imprisonment and humiliation; Joseph chooses prison over sin.
rows.anchor: اختار السجن على المعصية

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says servants were called fatā and the attendants may have been young or old; women servants were called fatāt.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: كانوا يسمون المملوك فتى فجائز أن يكون الفتيان حدثين أو شيخين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʾwīl reports what is present through the outcome of the unseen; it also denotes the meaning to which a text returns.
rows.anchor: التأويل الخبر عما حضر بما يؤول إليه أمره فيما غاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Teaching may impart evidence leading to knowledge or place knowledge in the heart; following means tracing another's path.
rows.anchor: والتعليم تفهيم الدلالة المؤدية إلى العلم بالمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated hum is emphatic: intervening 'hereafter' makes the first almost void and the second controls.
rows.anchor: هم الثانية دخلت للتوكيد لأنه لما دخل بينهما قوله { بالآخرة } صارت الأولى كالملغاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pattern also occurs in Luqman 31:4 and al-Muʾminun 23:35.
rows.anchor: وهم بالآخرة هم يوقنون

rows.speaker: قتادة والسدي
rows.claim: They say the two attendants served Egypt's greater king, Walid ibn Rayyan; one served drink and the other food, and the latter was suspected of poisoning him.
rows.anchor: وكان أحدهما صاحب شرابه والآخر صاحب طعامه فنمى إليه أن صاحب طعامه يريد أن يسمه

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud says the attendants invented dreams to test Joseph, who had offered to interpret dreams in prison.
rows.anchor: هلم فلنجربه فسألاه من غير أن يكونا رأيا شيئا عن ابن مسعود

rows.speaker: مجاهد والجبائي
rows.claim: Mujahid and al-Jubba'i say the dreams were genuine but the attendants lied when denying them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بل رؤياهما على صحة وحقيقة ولكنهما كذبا في الإنكار

rows.speaker: أبو مجلز
rows.claim: Abu Mijlaz says only the attendant who was crucified lied; the other's dream was true.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن المصلوب منهما كان كاذبا والآخر صادقا عن أبي مجلز

rows.speaker: صاحب الشراب
rows.claim: The cupbearer dreamed of a vine with three grape clusters, which he pressed into the king's cup and served.
rows.anchor: رأيت أصل حبلة عليها ثلاثة عناقيد من عنب فجنيتها وعصرتها في كأس الملك

rows.speaker: الزجاج وابن الأنباري
rows.claim: They explain 'press wine' by an omitted noun, grapes destined to become wine; Arabic can name something by what it becomes.
rows.anchor: العرب تسمي الشيء باسم ما يؤول إليه إذا وضح المعنى ولم يلتبس

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says the phrase means pressing grapes; some Arabs call grapes khamr.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: إن بعض العرب يسمون العنب خمرا

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Asma'i relates that Muʿtamir ibn Sulayman met a Bedouin carrying grapes who called them wine.
rows.anchor: حكى الأصمعي عن المعتمر بن سليمان أنه لقي أعرابيا معه عنب

rows.speaker: عبد الله وأبي
rows.claim: A reading attributed to ʿAbd Allah and Ubayy explicitly says Joseph saw himself pressing grapes.
rows.anchor: وروي في قراءة عبد الله وأبي جميعا إني رأيتني أعصر عنبا

rows.speaker: صاحب الطعام
rows.claim: The food attendant dreamed of three baskets of bread and other foods on his head, with birds of prey eating from them.
rows.anchor: فوق رأسي ثلاث سلال فيها الخبز وألوان الأطعمة وسباع الطير تنهش منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nabbiʾna bi-taʾwīlih means tell us its interpretation and outcome.
rows.anchor: أي أخبرنا بتعبيره وما يؤول إليه أمره

rows.speaker: الضحاك وأبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak and Abu Abd Allah report Joseph made room for crowded prisoners, helped the needy, and cared for the sick.
rows.anchor: كان إذا ضاق على رجل مكانه وسع له وإن احتاج جمع له وإن مرض قام عليه

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says Joseph aided the wronged and weak and visited the sick; another interpretation makes muhsinīn skilled dream interpreters.
rows.anchor: جاء في التفسير أنه كان يعين المظلوم وينصر الضعيف ويعود العليل

rows.speaker: الحديث
rows.claim: A prophetic report says true dreams are one part in forty-six of prophethood because both disclose what will happen.
rows.anchor: إن الرؤيا جزء من ستة وأربعين جزءا من النبوة

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم وابن أبي إسحاق
rows.claim: They read the prisoners' words as saying Joseph would be good to them if he interpreted their dreams.
rows.anchor: نراك من المحسنين إلينا إن فسرت لنا الرؤيا

rows.speaker: السدي وابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Joseph avoided immediately revealing the dreams because one involved affliction, and shifted to another subject.
rows.anchor: كره أن يخبرهما بالتأويل لما على أحدهما فيه من البلاء

rows.speaker: الحسن والجبائي
rows.claim: They say Joseph first mentioned foreknowledge of food to show his prophetic gift and win acceptance, as Jesus foretold what people ate and stored.
rows.anchor: إنما قدم هذا ليعلما ما خصه الله تعالى به من النبوة وليقبلا عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph would tell them while awake the interpretation of food seen in their dreams before it arrived.
rows.anchor: في اليقظة { قبل أن يأتيكما } التأويل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God teaches by placing knowledge in the heart, revelation, or evidence from which knowledge follows.
rows.anchor: قد يكون بأن يفعل العلم في قلبه وقد يكون بالوحي وقد يكون بنصب الأدلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only sincere believers merit this high rank; Joseph left a people denying God and the hereafter.
rows.anchor: لا يستحق هذه الرتبة الخطيرة إلا المؤمنون المخلصون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph followed the law of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; the prophetic household should worship only God.
rows.anchor: أي لا ينبغي لنا ونحن معدن النبوة وأهل بيت الرسالة أن ندين بغير التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The favor can mean monotheism and rejecting idolatry, or prophethood and knowledge; God favored the prophets and people through their mission.
rows.anchor: بأن خصنا بها وعلى الناس أيضا بإرسالنا إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people do not thank God; Joseph called these idolaters to monotheism once they were receptive.
rows.anchor: نعم الله تعالى وقد كان يوسف ع فيما بينهم زمانا

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ calls it an obscure shift to quote one speaker and then move to another without introducing the new voice, as in the linked passages.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء وهذا من أغمض ما يأتي في الكلام أن يحكي عن واحد ثم يعدل إلى شيء آخر

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i says the words belong to the wife: her confession lets Joseph know she did not falsely blame him in his absence, although she betrayed him face-to-face.
rows.anchor: ذلك الإقرار ليعلم يوسف أني لم أخنه في غيبته بتوريك الذنب عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not guide the schemes of those who betray trust.
rows.anchor: أي لا يهديهم في كيدهم ومكرهم

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most exegetes attribute 'I do not acquit myself' to Joseph.
rows.anchor: هذا من كلام يوسف عند أكثر المفسرين

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i instead attributes it to the wife, who does not absolve herself of evil and betrayal in Joseph's affair.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بل هو من كلام امرأة العزيز عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul persistently urges evil through desire; the article can refer to all souls generically or to this particular soul.
rows.anchor: والألف واللام للجنس فيكون المعنى أن كل النفوس كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā in 'except what my Lord has mercy on' may mean the person God protects by grace, as in 4:3.
rows.anchor: ما عصم ربي ومن قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Joseph speaks, he disclaims natural impulses and desires, not a resolve to sin, and credits his abstention to God's power, grace, and guidance.
rows.anchor: ولم يرد العزم على المعصية أي لا أبرئ نفسي مما لا تعرى منه طباع البشر

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says Joseph phrased this to avoid praising himself.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن إنما قال { وما أبرئ نفسي } لأنه كره أن يكون قد زكى نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is forgiving toward His servants and merciful to them.
rows.anchor: بعباده: { رحيم } بهم

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir reads nashā with nūn; the other canonical readers use yāʾ.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير حيث نشاء بالنون والباقون بالياء

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: For yāʾ, yashāʾ is third person like yatabawwaʾu; 39:74 supports the form.
rows.anchor: من قرأ بالياء فيشاء مسند إلى الغائب كما أن

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: With nūn, God's will can be stated although Joseph chooses in practice, since God empowers him, like the statement that God threw when the Prophet threw.
rows.anchor: جاز أن ينسب إلى الله وإن كانت ليوسف في المعنى

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Alternatively the dwelling may be a place of worship and nearness to God, making Joseph's stay a devotional act.
rows.anchor: أن يكون الموضع المتبوأ موضع نسك وقرب فالمكث فيه قربة إلى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in 'enabled Joseph' may work like lām in raddifa lakum and lillruʾyā taʿburūn; 46:26 has a comparable construction without lām.
rows.anchor: فيجوز أن يكون على حد التي في قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yatabawwaʾu is accusative as a circumstantial qualifier; ḥaythu may be an adverb or direct object, as al-Shammakh's verse shows.
rows.anchor: في موضع نصب على الحال تقديره مكناه متبوءا حيث يشاء

rows.speaker: الشماخ
rows.claim: Al-Shammakh's line supports ḥaythu as an accusative object.
rows.anchor: يرضى حيث تكبو النواحز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istikhlāṣ is making something exclusively one's own; makīn is one of standing and influence; tabawwuʾ is taking a home to which one returns.
rows.anchor: والتبوء اتخاذ منزل يرجع إليه وأصله من باء يبوء إذا رجع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king learned Joseph's integrity and innocence and wanted him as an exclusive counselor for state affairs.
rows.anchor: معناه أن الملك لما تبين له أمانة يوسف وبراءته من السوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text elides the messenger's arrival, Joseph's release and their meeting; the conversation showed his intelligence and trustworthiness.
rows.anchor: فلما جاء الرسول يوسف ودعاه خرج من السجن ودخل على الملك وكلمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Makīn means influential in rank and command; amīn means trustworthy and reliable.
rows.anchor: ذو مكانة متمكن في المنزلة والقدر نافذ القول والأمر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the king empowered Joseph over the realm like his own sovereign and entrusted it to him.
rows.anchor: مكنتك من ملكي وجعلت سلطانك فيه كسلطاني

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says the messenger brought new clothes; Joseph was thirty, and the king recognized the dream's interpretation and seated him before telling the dream.
rows.anchor: فأقبل يوسف وتنظف من درن السجن ولبس ثيابه وأتى الملك وهو يومئذ ابن ثلاثين سنة

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb says Joseph prayed that good hearts be turned toward prisoners and that news not be hidden from them; he described prison as graves of the living, sorrow, tested friends, and enemies' gloating.
rows.anchor: اللهم اعطف عليهم بقلوب الأخيار ولا تعم عليهم الأخبار

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb relates Joseph's prayers at the palace gate and before meeting the king, followed by greetings in Arabic and Hebrew.
rows.anchor: ولما دخل على الملك قال اللهم إني أسألك بخيرك من خيره

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: The king spoke seventy languages and Joseph answered each in kind; Joseph then described the seven fat cows, seven lean cows, and ears of grain in the king's dream.
rows.anchor: وكان الملك يتكلم بسبعين لسانا فكلما كلم يوسف بلسان أجابه بذلك اللسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph advises growing and storing grain in the seven fertile years, keeping stalks as fodder and saving a fifth to feed Egypt and surrounding lands during famine.
rows.anchor: أرى أن تجمع الطعام وتزرع زرعا كثيرا في هذه السنين المخصبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite 'earth' means the king's land; Joseph asks to guard its storehouses from betrayal and allocate grain to those entitled.
rows.anchor: يعني اجعلني على خزائن أرضك حافظا وواليا

rows.speaker: قتادة وابن إسحاق والجبائي
rows.claim: They explain ḥafīẓ as guarding entrusted goods and ʿalīm as knowing who is entitled so provisions are properly allocated.
rows.anchor: حافظ لما استودعتني لحفظه عن أن تجري فيه خيانة

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb interprets ḥafīẓ ʿalīm as skilled in writing and accounting.
rows.anchor: وقيل: حفيظ عليم أي كاتب حاسب عن وهب

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says Joseph could plan for famine years and know when hunger would start.
rows.anchor: حفيظ للتقدير في هذه السنين الجدبة عليم بوقت الجوع حين يقع عن الكلبي

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says Joseph could keep accounts and speak visitors' different languages.
rows.anchor: حفيظ للحساب عالم بالألسن وذلك أن الناس يفدون من كل ناحية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person may state his merits to an uninformed authority when it enables public benefit; this is not forbidden self-purification.
rows.anchor: يجوز للإنسان أن يصف نفسه بالفضل عند من لا يعرفه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One report says the king transferred Egypt's government to Joseph and removed Qiftir from office.
rows.anchor: فوض إليه أمر مصر ودخل بيته وعزل قطفير

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One report says Qiftir died and the king married Joseph to Raʿil, whom Joseph found a virgin; she bore him Ephraim and Misha.
rows.anchor: أن قطفير هلك في تلك الليالي فزوج الملك يوسف راعيل امرأة قطفير

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another report says Joseph did not marry her; she praised God after seeing his procession and remained in his household until death.
rows.anchor: إنه لم يتزوجها يوسف وأنها لما رأته في موكبه بكت

rows.speaker: علي بن إبراهيم بن هاشم
rows.claim: Ali ibn Ibrahim's tafsir recounts Joseph restoring the impoverished former ruler's widow's youth and marrying her as a virgin.
rows.anchor: فسأل الله فرد عليها فتزوجها وهي بكر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس عن رسول الله
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas attributes to the Prophet that Joseph would have been appointed immediately had he not asked for the storehouses, but his appointment was delayed a year.
rows.anchor: رحم الله أخي يوسف لو لم يقل اجعلني على خزائن الأرض لولاه من ساعته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: After a year, the king invested Joseph with office and regalia; Joseph ruled justly and became beloved.
rows.anchor: فلما انصرمت السنة من يوم سأل الإمارة دعاه الأمير فتوجه ورداه بسيفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God enabled Joseph to act throughout Egypt and grant religion and worldly blessings; the reward is for the obedient, or the patient according to Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: أي يتصرف فيها حيث يشاء وينزل منها حيث يشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hereafter's reward is purer than worldly power and free of its blemishes, better than Joseph's earthly kingdom.
rows.anchor: لخلوصه عن الشوائب والأقذار

rows.speaker: مجاهد وغيره
rows.claim: Mujahid and others say Joseph invited the king to Islam and the king and many people accepted.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه دعا الملك إلى الإسلام فأسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph could take office under idolatrous rulers to command right, forbid wrong, and place people's rights properly as prophet and imam.
rows.anchor: يتمكن بذلك من الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر ووضع الحقوق مواضعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Office let him call people to good and reunite with his family; the verse permits judging under a tyrant when religious law can be upheld.
rows.anchor: سبب يتوصل به إلى الدعاء إلى الخير وإلى رؤية والديه واخوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His rule was by God's grace and independent of the king's commands; Joseph exercised his own choice.
rows.anchor: دلالة على أن تصرفه كان باختياره من غير رجوع إلى الملك

rows.speaker: الرضا
rows.claim: A report in Kitāb al-Nubuwwa says Joseph stored grain for seven fertile years then exchanged it during famine for money, jewels, livestock, servants, property, lands, rivers, and finally the people's freedom, bringing all under his authority.
rows.anchor: سمعت الرضا ع يقول:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph says he rescued Egyptians to help rather than make them suffer, then freed them and restored their goods and servants and returned the king's ring, throne, and crown.
rows.anchor: فإني لم أصلحهم لأفسدهم ولم أنجهم من البلاء لأكون بلاء عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king agrees to follow Joseph's conduct and judgment and professes that God is one and Joseph His messenger.
rows.anchor: وأنا أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له وأنك رسوله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One report says Joseph never ate his fill in famine, fearing he would forget the hungry if he became full.
rows.anchor: أخاف أن أشبع فأنسى الجياع

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة غير أبي بكر
rows.claim: Kufans except Abu Bakr read li-fityānihi; the others read li-fityatihi.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة غير أبي بكر لفتيانه والباقون لفتيته

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali says fitwa marks a small number and fityān a larger number, though the patterns may substitute where sound form permits.
rows.anchor: الفتية جمع فتى في عدد القليل والفتيان في الكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jihāz means household goods or travel equipment, including a woman's trousseau; riḥāl are containers or dwellings, originally travel gear and camel saddles.
rows.anchor: جهاز البيت متاعه وجهزت فلانا هيأت جهاز سفره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob sends ten sons for food but keeps Benjamin; Joseph recognizes them, while they fail to recognize him after forty years and his rise to kingship.
rows.anchor: دخلوا عليه وهم عشرة وأمسك ابن يامين أخا يوسف لأمه فعرفهم يوسف وأنكروه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says forty years passed since Joseph was thrown in the well; royal clothes and status made recognition unlikely.
rows.anchor: وكان بين أن قذفوه في الجب وبين أن دخلوا عليه أربعين سنة

rows.speaker: علي بن إبراهيم
rows.claim: In Ali ibn Ibrahim's tafsir the brothers say they are needy Syrian shepherds, deny being spies, and appeal to Jacob's prophetic family and grief over the youngest brother, supposedly eaten by a wolf.
rows.anchor: نحن قوم من أرض الشام رعاة أصابنا الجهد فجئنا نمتار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brothers say Jacob kept Benjamin, the youngest and Joseph's full brother, at home for consolation after Joseph's loss.
rows.anchor: لأنه أخو الذي هلك من أمه فأبونا يتسلى به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph demands their paternal brother as proof; they promise to persuade their grieving father, and Simeon is kept as hostage by lot or because he had judged Joseph most fairly.
rows.anchor: فائتوني بأخيكم الذي من أبيكم إن كنتم صادقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jihāz is the grain loaded for each man, a camel-load; Joseph says he gives full measure and is the best host or best at assigning proper places.
rows.anchor: يعني حمل لكل رجل منهم بعيرا بعدتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Benjamin is not brought, they will receive no grain and may not approach Joseph's home or land.
rows.anchor: أي ليس لكم عندي طعام أكيله عليكم والمراد بالكيل المكيل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses their promise as coaxing or tricking Jacob until he sends Benjamin.
rows.anchor: معناه نستخدعه عنه حتى يخرجه معنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph uses a Hebrew-speaking interpreter so the brothers will not recognize him; shame might otherwise make them leave without bringing Benjamin.
rows.anchor: وكان يوسف أمر ترجمانا يعرف العبرانية أن يكلمهم

rows.speaker: قتادة وغيره
rows.claim: Joseph tells the grain-measuring servants to return the payment; another view says he ordered his assistants.
rows.anchor: قال يوسف لعبيده وغلمانه الذين يكيلون الطعام عن قتادة وغيره

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The brothers' payment may have been sandals and leather, or silver according to Qatada.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كانت بضاعتهم النعال والأدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph hoped the brothers would recognize their payment and return; he also considered it ungenerous to take money from needy relatives.
rows.anchor: إنه رأى لؤما أخذ ثمن الطعام من أبيه وإخوته مع حاجتهم إليه

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says Joseph feared they lacked enough silver to return for another grain trip.
rows.anchor: ما يرجعون به مرة أخرى عن الكلبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also knew their honesty would prompt them to return the payment once they found it, unaware the ruler had placed it there.
rows.anchor: علم أن ديانتهم وأمانتهم تحملهم على رد بضاعتهم إذا وجدوها في رحالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabrisi prefers that Joseph was not permitted to reveal himself until the divinely intended trial ended; alternatively, he wanted the brothers to return with Benjamin.
rows.anchor: والأول هو الوجه الصحيح

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة غير عاصم
rows.claim: Kufans except Asim read yaktal with yāʾ; the others read naktal with nūn.
rows.anchor: قرأ يكتل بالياء أهل الكوفة غير عاصم والباقون بالنون

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة غير أبي بكر
rows.claim: Kufans except Abu Bakr read ḥāfiẓan; others have ḥifẓan, and Ibn ʿAlqama and Yahya anomalously read ruddati with kasra.
rows.anchor: وقرأ خير حافظا بالألف أهل الكوفة غير أبي بكر والباقون حفظا بغير ألف

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Nūn matches their promise to provide for family, protect Benjamin, and gain another load; it may include Benjamin in measuring, while yāʾ means he takes his own load.
rows.anchor: يدل على النون في نكتل قوله { ونمير أهلنا ونحفظ أخانا ونزداد كيل بعير }

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: A reading from ʿAbd Allah has nūn because they were denied grain in their brother's absence and expect it when he arrives.
rows.anchor: وزعموا أن في قراءة عبد الله نكتل بالنون

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Noun ḥifẓ refers to the weak protection claimed by the brothers; God is the better guardian, as with partners falsely attributed to Him.
rows.anchor: فالله خير حفظا من حفظكم الذي نسبتموه إلى أنفسكم

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Ḥāfiẓan may be specification or circumstantial; unlike the noun construction it can be annexed in 'best guardian.'
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ حافظا فيكون خافظا منتصبا على التمييز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Doubled verbs most strongly take initial damma, then a mixed vowel, rarely pure kasra; hollow verbs have a corresponding hierarchy beginning with kasra.
rows.anchor: فأقوى اللغات في المضاعف ضم أوله كشد وعد ورد

rows.speaker: ذو الرمة
rows.claim: Dhu al-Rumma's verse illustrates the rare kasra reading ruddati.
rows.anchor: دنا البين من مي فردت جمالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kiltu means give by measure, iktaltu means take by measure, and mīra is food carried from one place to another.
rows.anchor: يقال كلت فلانا أي أعطيته الشيء كيلا واكتلت عليه أخذت منه

rows.speaker: الشعر
rows.claim: The poem uses māʾiran for a person sent to fetch provisions.
rows.anchor: بعثتك مائرا فمكثت حولا

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says ḥifẓan is a specification and ḥāfiẓan can be circumstantial or specifying; mā nabghī may ask rhetorically what they seek or negate their seeking anything.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج حفظا منصوب على التمييز وحافظا على الحال

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: The exception permits inability to bring Benjamin if wholly surrounded; illa can also affirm a resulting condition, as when one comes only to collect money.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج وإلا هذه بمعنى تحقيق الجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob notes their weak greeting and Simeon's absence; the brothers praise Egypt's ruler and explain grain will be withheld next time without Benjamin.
rows.anchor: يا بني ما لكم تسلمون سلاما ضعيفا وما لي لا أسمع فيكم صوت شمعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naktal means the brothers receive measured grain if Benjamin comes; yaktal means Benjamin measures his own camel-load.
rows.anchor: نأخذ الطعام بالكيل إن أرسلته أكتلنا وإلا فمنعنا الكيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their promise to guard Benjamin recalls their failed claim about Joseph, which Jacob invokes although he knows they would not now do wrong.
rows.anchor: لا آمنكم على ابن يامين في الذهاب به إلا كأمني على يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's protection surpasses theirs; a report says God promised Jacob to return both sons after his trust in Him.
rows.anchor: فبعزتي لأردنهما إليك من بعد ما توكلت علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'What more do we seek?' may mean they are not lying about Egypt's ruler.
rows.anchor: ما نطلب بما أخبرناك عن ملك مصر الكذب

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada reads 'what more do we seek?' as receiving full measure and having their payment returned.
rows.anchor: أي شيء نطلب وراء هذا أوفى لنا الكيل ورد علينا الثمن عن قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The returned payment means there is no reason to fear the ruler's kindness; alternatively, it will cover the next journey without Jacob's money.
rows.anchor: أي فلا ينبغي أن نخاف على أخينا ممن قد أحسن إلينا هذا الإحسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They promise to bring food, protect Benjamin, and gain his additional camel-load because each man got one load.
rows.anchor: لأجله لأنه كان يكال لكل رجل وقر بعير

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the measure is easy for the king and does not strain his resources.
rows.anchor: عن الزجاج والمعنى أنه هين على الملك لا يصعب عليه ولا يظهر في ماله

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i says their grain amount is too small, so they need Benjamin's load too.
rows.anchor: كيل قليل لا يقنعنا فنحتاج أن نضيف إليه كيل بعير أخينا عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says it is easy for the person measuring, with no expense or hardship.
rows.anchor: يسير على من يكتاله لا مؤنة فيه ولا مشقة عن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the kindness is confirmed, Jacob requires a solemn covenant in God's name that they bring Benjamin back.
rows.anchor: قال لن أرسله معكم حتى تؤتون موثقا من الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Jacob required an oath invoking Muhammad, the final and chief of messengers.
rows.anchor: بحق محمد خاتم النبيين صلى الله عليه وسلم وسيد المرسلين

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid reads the exception as all brothers perishing.
rows.anchor: إلا أن تهلكوا جميعا عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says it means they are overpowered and cannot fulfill their promise.
rows.anchor: إلا أن تغلبوا حتى لا تطيقوا ذلك عن قتادة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj interprets it as being prevented from bringing Benjamin.
rows.anchor: حتى لا تقدروا على الإتيان به عن الزجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob declares God witness and protector who will vindicate him if they break the oath; the verse teaches reliance on God in important matters.
rows.anchor: أي شاهد حافظ إن أخلفتم انتصف لي منكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob now trusted them because they had grown up, regretted their past treatment of Joseph, and no longer persisted in wrongdoing; he invoked Joseph to urge care for Benjamin.
rows.anchor: وإنما عيرهم بحديث يوسف حثا لهم على حفظ أخيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghinā means financial sufficiency; long-vowel ghināʾ is singing, and related forms mean residing or being content.
rows.anchor: الغنى الكفاية في المال لأنه اكتفى به وربما مد لضرورة الشعر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة والضحاك والسدي وأبو مسلم
rows.claim: These authorities say Jacob feared the evil eye because his sons were handsome and imposing, so he told them to enter through separate gates.
rows.anchor: خاف عليهم العين لأنهم كانوا ذوي جمال وهيئة وكمال

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i rejects the evil eye and says Jacob feared envy of the brothers' strength leading the king to imprison or kill them.
rows.anchor: خاف عليهم حسد الناس إياهم وإن يبلغ الملك قوتهم وبطشهم

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i says the evil eye lacks proof; many scholars accept it and cite the Prophet saying it can bring down a high mountain.
rows.anchor: وأنكر العين وذكر أنه لم يثبت بحجة وجوزه كثير من المحققين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥāliq is a high place on a mountain; the report compares the eye's power to bringing down a summit.
rows.anchor: العين كأنها تحط ذروة الجبل من قوة أخذها وشدة بطشها

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet's prayer for Hasan and Husayn seeks God's protection from devils, poisonous creatures, and every blameworthy eye.
rows.anchor: أعيذكما بكلمات الله التامة من كل شيطان وهامة ومن كل عين لامة

rows.speaker: إبراهيم وموسى
rows.claim: Reports say Abraham used the prayer for his sons and Moses for Aaron's two sons.
rows.anchor: وروي أن إبراهيم ع عوذ ابنيه وإن موسى عوذ ابني هارون بهذه العوذة

rows.speaker: أسماء بنت عميس
rows.claim: Asma bint Umays asks to seek protection for Jaʿfar's fair-skinned sons because the eye affects them quickly; the Prophet approves.
rows.anchor: يا رسول الله إن العين إليهم سريعة أفأسترقي لهم من العين

rows.speaker: جبرائيل
rows.claim: Gabriel recited and taught the Prophet a prayer for healing from every envious eye.
rows.anchor: بسم الله أرقيك من كل عين حاسد الله يشفيك

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A prophetic report says that if anything could precede destiny, it would be the evil eye.
rows.anchor: لو كان شيء يسبق القدر لسبقته العين
